subject: [GlyphTech] Capacity bridging plan + interim update after GPU eviction spike
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: ops-team@glyphtech.com, laura.connors@glyphtech.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: [GlyphTech] Capacity bridging plan + interim update after GPU eviction spike

Laura / GlyphTech SRE team —

Thanks again for the quick calls this morning. Short summary up front: during the 08:30–08:50 PDT window your Dedicated pool experienced a short eviction storm that reduced available slots by ~30% for ~18 minutes, which transiently increased request latency and led to several 5xx errors on a small subset of routes. We believe the root proximate cause was a combination of a sudden burst of very short-context generation jobs from one of your microservices plus aggressive autoscaler cooldown settings that delayed additional node provisioning.

Immediate mitigation we applied:
- Provisioned two hot-standby nodes into your pool (temporary reserved nodes) to restore capacity headroom.
- Enabled conservative autoscale override for your pool (lowered cooldown from 300s to 60s for next 24h).
- Activated per-customer KV-prefix caching to reduce re-computation for repeated short prompts.

Next steps we are executing now (ETA timelines below):
- Engineering: full incident triage and postmortem draft by EOD PT today (ETA 18:00 PDT).
- Ops: keep the two hot-standby nodes until 2027-06-20 08:00 PDT to validate traffic normalization.
- Account: we'll propose a one-time credit to compensate for the affected window once we confirm token counts (aiming to share proposed credit by EOD tomorrow).

If you can share any internal spike logs (timestamped request IDs or a histogram of request durations around 08:20–09:00), that would help us correlate. For transparency I've looped in Marissa (engineer) and Dylan (support) who are preparing the technical notes and customer-facing comms.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll keep you updated every 2–3 hours until the situation is fully stabilized.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment (referenced): incident-runbook-changes.md (summary of temporary autoscale override)
From: SRE Team <sre@glyphtech.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [GlyphTech] Capacity bridging plan + interim update after GPU eviction spike

Vivek —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the hot-standby nodes. We pulled logs for the window and attached two artifacts: request-id dump and per-instance memory/CPU traces. Quick observations from our side:
- The spike originated from a batch of ~1.2k requests to the /generate/short endpoint from our experimentation service at 08:22:34 PDT.
- These requests had unusually short target tokens (avg 12 tokens) but came as a high-rate burst — the kernel-level scheduler on the nodes had trouble filling batches efficiently and we saw elevated eviction counts.

Questions:
1) Is there a recommended config on your side to avoid eviction during short-token burst patterns?
2) Will the temporary autoscale override impact our normal cost reporting for the month?

We'll hold off on scaling down until you give the all-clear.

— GlyphTech SRE (Ben Franklin)
Attachment (referenced): glyphtech-request-ids-0822.log
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: sre@glyphtech.com, vivek@redwood.ai
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [GlyphTech] Capacity bridging plan + interim update after GPU eviction spike

Ben / Laura / team —

Thanks for the artifacts — very helpful. Quick technical write-up so you have the engineering view in one place:

What happened (short):
- A high-rate burst of very short-context requests overloaded the per-node batch scheduler. Because batch fill is low for short-context jobs, the scheduler increased concurrency which pushed memory pressure on the GPU. Our eviction policy kicked in to free KV cache space, which caused a cascade of warm caches becoming cold and additional compute load. The autoscaler was in a cooldown state from a prior downscale, which delayed node add.

Immediate mitigations applied (what you saw):
- Two hot-standby nodes seeded to restore headroom.
- Temporarily lowered downscale cooldown to allow faster node addition.
- Enabled per-customer soft rate limiting at the edge for /generate/short for 20 minutes to smooth the burst (rate cap set to 300 rps).

Recommended long-term mitigations (proposed):
- Add a short-request lane: a small dedicated pool sized for short-context bursty workloads with tighter batching parameters (smaller max_batch but faster batch windows).
- Expose per-route autoscale profiles so you can pin more aggressive scale-up behavior for critical endpoints.
- Improve eviction policy heuristics to consider request-rate anomalies and avoid cascade evictions during transient bursts.

Status & timeline:
- Postmortem draft is attached (glyphtech_postmortem_v1.pdf). Please review and flag anything you want emphasized.
- We'll propose the dedicated short-request lane configuration and cost estimate by Monday 2027-06-21.

Let me know if you'd like a 30-min tech working session to walk the proposed lane configuration.

-Marissa
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: glyphtech_postmortem_v1.pdf
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: laura.connors@glyphtech.com, ops-team@glyphtech.com
Cc: vivek@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 14:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [GlyphTech] Capacity bridging plan + interim update after GPU eviction spike

Laura / team —

I wanted to follow up quickly on the account-side items:
- We'll calculate the token and request counts for the outage window and share a proposed credit. Our preliminary estimate is a one-off credit equivalent to ~8 hours of dedicated pool usage (we'll confirm exact $ amount by EOD Monday).
- The temporary hot-standby nodes will be billed at a reduced rate per our incident credit policy; we'll net that into the proposed credit rather than charging you full price.
- If you accept the recommendation for a short-request lane (Marissa's note), we can prepare both a 30-day pilot pricing sheet and a full committed plan for Dedicated.

If you'd like the account team to join the tech working session, we can bring pricing scenarios and cost/benefit analysis.

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: laura.connors@glyphtech.com, sre@glyphtech.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 19 Jun 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: [GlyphTech] Final postmortem summary, actions, and next steps (incident closed)

Laura / Ben / GlyphTech team —

Attached is the final incident summary and the action-items tracker. Highlights and closure notes:

Root cause (condensed):
- Short bursts of high-rate, short-context requests caused inefficient batching and transient GPU memory pressure. Eviction policy + autoscaler cooldown combined to create a capacity gap.

What we did (timeline):
- 08:25 PDT: detected eviction alarm and elevated error rates.
- 08:28 PDT: notification to account + ops; applied hot-standby nodes and enabled per-route edge smoothing.
- 08:46 PDT: error rates returned to baseline; continued monitoring.

Permanent action items (owners & ETA):
- Marissa: implement a dedicated short-request lane prototype and run internal load tests (ETA 2027-07-08).
- Dylan: update customer Runbook and add a short-request mitigation checklist (ETA 2027-06-25).
- EngInfra: refine autoscaler cooldown logic to allow emergency scale-up bypass for eviction alarms (JIRA SERV-821) (ETA 2027-07-15).
- Hannah / Accounts: prepare pilot pricing for 30-day short-request lane (ETA 2027-06-21).

Credits & commercial: Hannah will circulate the exact credit amount; our offer includes billing relief for the hot-standby nodes plus an incident credit.

Status: incident considered closed as of 2027-06-19 15:00 PDT, pending your acceptance of the proposed action items and the pilot package. If you want any edits to the postmortem PDF, tell us and we'll incorporate immediately.

Thanks for the partnership and for sharing detailed traces — that made the investigation much faster.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: glyphtech_postmortem_v1.pdf, incident-runbook-changes.md
